A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PMC research, with matching core methods, experiments and theoretical appendices. All 23 pages of v3 and 37 pages of v4, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original TOFU unlearning experiments, utility evaluations, attack tests, ablations and categorical/Gaussian-mixture simulations.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds Gemma experiments, a MUSE-news pilot, and runtime, reward and checkpointing analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 remains unchanged, but v4 substantially extends the implemented procedures: PMC-fast selects reward-improving samples and stops sampling at maximum reward; additional variants use restarts and self-BLEU rewards. Appendix A.10 also adapts PMC to sentence continuations from randomly selected prefixes. These are actual procedural additions, not merely expanded explanations.

E1.justification: v4 adds MUSE-news-small, containing 454 forget and 1,714 retain sentences, alongside the retained TOFU experiments. This extends LLM unlearning from fictional-author question answering to news sentences using continuation training (Appendix A.10). The existing utility benchmarks and synthetic simulations are retained.

E2.justification: v4 adds DPO to the Phi/Llama TOFU comparisons, epoch ablation and sampling/prefilling evaluation (Figures 3, 4 and 6). The existing GA, GD, NPO, SimNPO and IDK comparators remain. The new Gemma comparison explicitly excludes DPO and NPO because of their reference-model costs.

E3.justification: v4 adds Gemma-3-12b-it configurations and a Llama-2-7b MUSE protocol using sentence-level training, ten epochs and KnowMem evaluation. It also introduces controlled H200 runtime comparisons and additional cross-model experimental settings. The retained TOFU split remains unchanged, while aggregate utility and unlearning scores are normalized by their maximum possible values.

E4.justification: Beyond v3's retained ablations and attacks, v4 adds detailed epoch/runtime sensitivity studies across three models, PMC-fast cost comparisons, empirical reward-convergence checks, alternative-reward tests and gradient-checkpointing ablations (Appendices A.2–A.9). The per-question leakage distributions in Appendix A.5 also examine variation hidden by the previously reported average.

E5.justification: Five-seed reporting remains for the retained Phi/Llama experiments. v4 identifies Gemma comparisons and Appendix B.4 analyses as single-run results, and replaces v3's five-run runtime summaries with individual trajectories. These disclosures do not establish reduced replication of retained experiments. Table 4 still lists five Gemma seeds, inconsistently with the single-run exception in Section 5.1.

E6.justification: v4 adds DPO and Gemma results, MUSE KnowMem outcomes and substantial diagnostic findings, including reported reward convergence within 50 training steps (Figure 25). Table 1 retains the Phi/Llama values and adds Gemma PMC scores of 0.6032, 0.8421 and 0.6934 for ARC-Challenge, ARC-Easy and MMLU. Changed runtime figures use different hardware/settings and therefore do not establish a same-setting speed improvement.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 now explicitly requires positive initial probability mass on maximum-reward responses for every forget query. v3 stated convergence without this support assumption. This substantively restricts the theorem's applicability; the categorical proofs, Theorem 2 and the remaining derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The central PMC, utility and robustness contributions remain. v4 refines the introductory privacy claim by dropping the assertion that PMC avoids private data in its objective and emphasizing independence from fixed ground-truth sequences instead. The change from three to four limitations does not establish another distinct contribution: sampling/prefilling robustness appears twice in the new enumeration.

C2.justification: v4 substantially expands the qualifications: outputs can become hallucinations, gibberish or empty responses; generated samples can initially contain sensitive information; and collapse requires accessible higher-reward responses. Section 6 distinguishes output removal from convergence to a retrained model and explicitly disclaims formal unlearning guarantees. The appendices add interpretations of utility drops, approximation trade-offs, checkpointing sensitivity and MUSE evaluation weaknesses.

D1.justification: v4 documents Gemma/DPO hyperparameters, hardware assignments and settings for the new runtime, reward and sensitivity experiments. Appendix A.10 specifies MUSE filtering and prefix-sampling details. It also clarifies greedy reference generation and utility evaluation without the TOFU chat template. Code access already existed in v3; v4 additionally states that experiment configurations are released with the code.

R1.justification: v4 adds the Gemma 3 report and Schwinn et al. (2025), removes Cao and Yang (2015), and clarifies positioning relative to distribution matching and alignment. IDK is attributed to Zhang et al. (2024), whereas v3 introduced it as a new baseline. The DPO reference's year/venue update concerns the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: The introduction, results explanations and Discussion receive substantial rewriting. Sampling/prefilling attacks move ahead of the side-effect analysis, Section 5.4 becomes a broader experimental overview, and the appendices gain navigation and reorganized experimental subsections. These narrative changes extend beyond inserting new scientific content.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to distinguish refusal fine-tuning from gradient ascent. Figure 3 expands from two to three panels with a shared legend and normalized axes; Figure 7 redisplays its data with accessible markers. Numerous diagnostic plots are added, attack/ablation displays gain DPO, and tables expand for Gemma. Several retained figures are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v4 makes PMC's mechanism, computational feasibility and failure conditions substantially more assessable. Compared with v3's brief runtime reporting and limited collapse diagnostics, it adds controlled cost trajectories, direct reward-convergence evidence and targeted reward/checkpointing analyses, alongside stronger comparator and model coverage. The explicit theorem assumption and clearer privacy and evaluation limitations improve precision. Single-run additions, seed/caption inconsistencies and the limited MUSE pilot temper the evidence, but the gains in empirical support and interpretation constitute a substantial overall improvement.
